ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Angle from an upward-pointing vertical line, measured in a vertical plane. A horizontal line has a zenith angle of 90 degrees

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Anisotropic Axis 1 Crossline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Angle of first (or only) anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the cross-line direction. Axis 1 on its own defines the rotational symmetry axis for transverse isotropy. If accompanied by Axis 2, they together define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Anisotropic Axis 1 Crossline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 crossline direction for a layer.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stack Anisotropic Axis 1 Crossline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 crossline direction for all layers to the current depth.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Anisotropic Axis 1 Inline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Angle of first (or only) anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the in-line direction. Axis 1 on its own defines the rotational symmetry axis for transverse isotropy. If accompanied by Axis 2, they together define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Anisotropic Axis 1 Inline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 inline direction for a layer.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stack Anisotropic Axis 1 Inline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 1 inline direction for all layers to the current depth.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Anisotropic Axis 2 Crossline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Angle of second anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the cross-line direction. Taken together with Axis 1, Axis 2 is used to define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Anisotropic Axis 2 Crossline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 crossline direction for a layer.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stack Anisotropic Axis 2 Crossline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 crossline direction for all layers to the current depth.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Anisotropic Axis 2 Inline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Angle of second anisotropic symmetry axis, relative to vertical, measured in the in-line direction. Taken together with Axis 1, Axis 2 is used to define the symmetry planes for orthorhombic anisotropy.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Anisotropic Axis 2 Inline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 inline direction for a layer.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stack Anisotropic Axis 2 Inline Direction
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 inline direction for all layers to the current depth.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inclination Error
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Plus or minus inclination error of sensor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Azimuth Error
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Plus or minus azimuth error of sensor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Hydraulic Power
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Power produced or available from a system due to fluid flow, such as for pumps and turbines.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cementing Unit Input Horse Power
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cementing unit input horse power

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Hydraulic Horse Power
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum hydraulic power (Flowrate x pressure) of a fluid. Often referred to Hydraulic horse power

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Pump Input Horse Power
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Mud pump input horse power.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Nominal Hydraulic Power
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Hydraulic (Flowrate x pressure) power that the equipment can sustain over a long period of time, as opposed to maximum working pressure which is the peak maximum

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Nanowatt
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Unit is always nW

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Electromagnetic Power
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate at which electromagnetic energy is emitted or transferred.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Energy Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Energy per unit time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the ability of a body to resist applied force.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Compressive Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The degree of resistance of a material to force acting along one of the axes in a manner tending to crush it.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Compressive Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The compressive strength of an earth formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fundamental Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The stress a material is able to withstand under a given set of conditions (temperature, pressure, solution, etc.) without deforming continuously.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Embedment Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Force required to push a 1/8 inch diameter sphere 1/16 in into the rock. (Lab test). Value ranges from 5 to 20 kpsi for chalk, 40 to 100 kpsi for sandstones, 50 to 200 for Dolomites.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tensile Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The maximum tensile stress a material can tolerate without splitting

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Barometric Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure of the atmosphere (relative to vacuum) as measured by a barometer

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Differential Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The difference between the pressures of two systems, or between the pressures measured at different points in a system.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gas Differential Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Gas differential pressure across the orifice plate when a sample is taken

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Max Differential Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum Differential Pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Elastic Modulus
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The stress-strain properties of isotropic materials which obeys Hooke's law, for small formations, are specified by elastic moduli.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bulk Modulus: k
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The stress-strain ratio under simple hydrostatic pressure. k = Delta-P / (Delta V / V), where Delta-P, -V denote the change in Pressure and Volume.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Frame Bulk Modulus
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The bulk modulus of the solid frame of the rock. The solid frame of the rock includes the porosity but not the content of the pore spaces.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shear/Rigidity/Lame Modulus: Mu
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The stress-strain ratio for simple shear. Also called rigidity modulus or Lame's constant.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Frame Shear Modulus
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The shear modulus of the solid frame of the rock. The solid frame of the rock includes the porosity but not the content of the pore spaces.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Young's Modulus
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The stress-strain ratio when a body is pulled or compressed.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gauge Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure above one atmosphere.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Activation Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at which recording should begin

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Air Supply Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Air supply pressure; for a burner, the pressure required to achieve effective atomization

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Annulus Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure of the fluid in the annulus. The annulus is the region outside the subject pipe, such as the region between drill pipe and the formation, or between casing and formation, or between tubing and casing.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Abandonment Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure at which a reservoir was or is expected to be abandoned.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Average Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure averaged on a given time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Average Reservoir Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The average pressure (somewhere in the reservoir) between the borehole pressure and external boundary pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Back Pressure Drop
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Constant pressure drop on a flowline used mainly to approximate any kind of restriction, choke, nozzle ...

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Capillary Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The difference in pressure between two phases, air fluid, gas fluid or between two fluids, measured at points of the interconnected phases.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottomhole Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure at the bottom of a borehole generally associated with the pore pressure of the formation open to the well.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottomhole Shut-in Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure at the bottom of a borehole with the well shut in.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Drawdown Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The difference in shut in and flowing bottomhole pressures, at a constant rate of fluid production.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Critical Drawdown Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The upper limit of drawdown pressure that can be applied to a completion system without causing damage to the system (such as erosion to a gravel pack completion system).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottomhole Circulating Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure at the bottom of a borehole during circulation of any fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottomhole Flowing Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flowing pressure inside the wellbore at midpoint of the completed interval. Res. Eng. Pwf

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Breakdown Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure required to create a hydraulic fracture in an unfractured formation; it is greater than fracture closure pressure except in rare cases, such as very low fracture toughness and very large horizontal stress anisotropy.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bubble Point Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure at reservoir temperature at which gas in solution in crude oil comes out of solution as free gas.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Buildup Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure recorded in the borehole at downhole conditions during a pressure buildup test.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Burst Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Burst Pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cementing Unit Max Discharge Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cementing unit maximum discharge pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Circulating Line Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure observed at circulating line/BOP

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Circulating Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Fluid pressure under circulating conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Collapse Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Collapse Pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Compression Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure applied to compress a body or material, as opposed to that applied by tension.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Critical Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure needed to condense a vapor at its critical temperature. Applies to pure components; for mixtures use Pseudocritical_Pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Critical Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure needed to condense a dry gas at its critical temperature (Dry gas = free gas without condensate)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pseudocritical Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure needed to condense the vapor of a gas mixture at its pseudocritical temperature. Analogous to Critical_Pressure for pure components.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wet Gas Critical Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure needed to condense a wet gas at its critical temperature (Wet gas : mixture of free gas plus condensate)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Dew Point Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure at which a liquid phase condenses from a vaporous fluid in equilibrium at a given temperature.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Downstream Coil Working Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Coil working pressure downstream of the choke box

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Downstream Orifice Gas Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure of gas separator gas line downstream of orifice plate when a sample is taken

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Elastic Limit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The greatest stress that can be applied to a body without causing permanent deformation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Engine Oil Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure of the lubrication oil

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Test Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Recommended pressure the equipment is tested when inspected or certified

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: External Boundary Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure existing at the external boundary of the drainage area of the well.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Extrapolated Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Extrapolated pressure from infinite-acting analysis

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Extrapolated Pressure - Spherical
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Extrapolated pressure from spherical flow analysis

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fann Test Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure at which the Fann test was performed.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fracture Closure Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Magnitude of the stress required to open a preexisting fracture. Assumed to be equal to the least principal stress which acts perpendicular to the face of the fracture, trying to keep it closed. Above it, the fracture is open, closed below.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Final Transfer Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Final pressure of shipping bottle

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Well Flowing Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure of the flowing well measured at the intake point in the borehole.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Frac Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Fluid pressure in the wellbore required to undergo hydraulic fracturing.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Hydraulic Drive Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure of the hydraulic fluid delivered to an Hydraulic motor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Hydrostatic Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure due to the weight of a column of liquid (formation water, drilling mud, etc.) extending from the depth of interest to the liquid level.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Liquid Head Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure, represented as the height of a column of dense fluid that can be supported by the pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Initial Reservoir Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Initial reservoir pressure, before any production or injection occurs, normally abbreviated Pi; sometimes taken as the pressure at the external boundary of the drainage area.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inlet Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at the inlet of an equipment item.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Kick Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure measurement used for kick detection.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Kill Line Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure observed at kill line/BOP.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Last Static Reservoir Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Last reservoir pressure recorded

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Max Allowable Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum allowable pressure for the equipment

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Lithostatic Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure produced by the weight of overlying rock. Also called Abnormal pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Max Allowable Surface Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum allowable mud surface pressure in annulus (drill-pipe x casing) to be used during well control operations so as not to exceed the FIT/LOT equivalent mud weight.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Gooseneck Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum pressure observed during a Coil Tubing job at the goose neck

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Operating Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum pressure which an equipment can withstand without permanent damage at standard temperature.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Outer Vessel Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum working pressure of the outer equipment

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Max Surge Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum pressure to which this Equipment can be exposed for a short time without permanent damage; the Equipment will again perform to specifications when the pressure is reduced below the maximum working pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Water Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum water pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Net Fracturing Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Hydraulic pressure exerted on a formation during a fracturing job (fracture pressure) minus Closure Pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Pump Maximum Discharge Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Mud pump maximum discharge pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Loss
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The difference between input and output pressure, usually due to friction.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Nominal Pressure Loss
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The nominal pressure loss in a piece of equipment, such as a Drill_Motor or an MWD_Tool.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Sensor Drift
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure difference over time in the gauge output with constant input conditions

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Sensor Noise
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Random changes in pressure sensor response.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Sensor Resolution
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The minimum significant pressure change that can be detected above the noise. This is measured as the standard deviation of the differences between two successive measurements.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Output Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at the output of an equipment item.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Overbalance Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The difference between formation pressure and the pressure of the fluid in the borehole.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Overburden Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure exerted on the matrix of a porous media by the weight of overlying strata.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pad Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure with which the pad of a logging or testing device is applied to the formation or other interface.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure At One hour
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure measured 1 hour after start of test.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pore Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure of the fluid contained in the pore volume.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Reference Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Reference Pressure, as for a PVT computation

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inlet Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at the inlet of a coiled tubing reel.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sandface Well Flowing Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pressure in the formation immediately prior to entering any completion pressure drops.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Separator Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure of the separator when a sample is taken

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Test Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Recommended pressure at which the equipment is tested when inspected or certified

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stress
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Force acting per unit area in a material resisting the stretching, compression or shear induced by external forces; fully characterized by a Stress_Tensor.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shear Stress
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Shear force (shear: strain that causes contiguous parts of a body to slide relatively to each other in a direction parallel to their plane of contact) per area unit of surface

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: 10 Minute Gel Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 10 minutes.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: 10 Second Gel Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 10 seconds.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: 1 Minute Gel Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 1 minute.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: 30 Minute Gel Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Shear Stress required to break a gel fluid previously allowed to remain at rest for 30 minutes.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Yield Point
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistance to initial flow; the stress required to start fluid movement. Specifically, shear stress at 0 shear rate for Bingham Plastic (BP) rheological model, otherwise named Bingham yield value or yield point. BP fluid remains static until applied forces build up to the point where it starts to move. See Plastic_Viscosity.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: API Yield Stress
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistance to initial flow; the stress required to start fluid movement. When using the direct-indicating viscometer, it is found by subtracting plastic viscosity (API_Plastic_Viscosity) from the 300-rpm reading of a Fann35 rheometer.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Casson Yield Stress
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistance to initial flow; the stress required to start fluid movement. The Casson model equation is: SQRT(Shear_Stress) = SQRT(Yield_Stress) + SQRT(Plastic_Viscosity X Shear_Rate)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stress Tensor
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A second rank tensor whose components are the stresses exerted across surfaces perpendicular to the coordinate directions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Von Mises Stress
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Normalized sum of the square of the differences of principal stresses applied to a material, e.g. for coiled tubing hoop, bending & radial. See Von_Mises_To_Yield_Ratio.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Eff Formation Stress
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Effective Stress of completed interval

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Minimum In Situ Stress
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Formation minimum principal stress, the smallest of the 3 components of the diagonal stress tensor (fractures will propagate perpendicular to its direction). Can be defaulted to Frac Gradient x TVD. Can be output from DataFRAC treatment.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Standard Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure considered to be "standard", for rates and volumes reported to be measured at Standard Conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Standpipe Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Mud pressure at the stand pipe manifold, just before the flexhose connecting to the swivel.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Static Potential
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Static (built up) pressure of a hydraulic unit, converted to pressure potential at a reference datum depth.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Static Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Static (non-flowing) Pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stiffness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The ratio of stress acting in a specified direction to the strain in a specified direction. Stiffness is a tensor of rank 4, but is expressible as a 6x6 matrix, the inverse of the compliance matrix.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Upstream Coil Working Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Coil working pressure upstream of the choke box

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure at End of Transient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at Transient End Time (pend)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure at Start of Transient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at start of Transient

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Vertical Lift Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Computed pressure at some depth in tubing

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wellhead Flowing Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at the Wellhead with well flowing

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wellhead Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The producing or shutin pressure at the top of the well before any surface pressure drops.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Static Wellhead Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Static wellhead pressure during test

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Working Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure at which an equipment item normally operates

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Choke Working Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Working pressure of the choke box which allow for the well fluid flow to be controlled by varying the flow cross-sectional area

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Working Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Recommended maximum pressure at which equipment can be used

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Yield Strength
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Unit stress which will produce a small amount of deformation generally equal to a strain of 0.2%. This value is a little greater than the Elastic limit. It is often supplied by the manufacturer of the material.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Membrane_Stiffness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Measurement of the stiffness of a membrane, such as mud filter cake.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mudcake Membrane Stiffness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Characterization of the flexibility of mudcake, defined as the ratio of the stress difference across the mudcake-formation boundary to the relative displacement between the pore fluid and the solid frame.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: MembraneStiffness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Measurement of the stiffness of a membrane, such as mud filter cake.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The change in pressure per unit length.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pore Pressure Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The change in pore pressure per unit length.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fracture Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Ratio of the Frac Pressure to the true vertical depth. Typical values for a reservoir range from 0.4-0.6 psi/ft for a depleted reservoir to 0.8-1.0 psi/ft for deep high pressure formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Pressure Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The Mud density expressed in pressure gradient. Usually used to compare the mud induced pressure with the pore and frac pressure.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stress Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Change in stress magnitude over distance.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the rate at which pressure varies per time; e.g., slider pressure correction.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Array Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Formation resistivity as measured by a device capable of taking measurements of at various combinations of resolution, depth of investigation and/or in different azimuthal directions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Array Induction Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Array Resistivity measurement using induction logging principles.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Array Laterolog Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Array Resistivity measurement using laterolog (or guard log) resistivity logging principles.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bound Water Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of water bound to clay in the formations.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Clay Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The Resistivity of clay, usually referring to that measured in the Earth formations.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Deep Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity which represents a measurement made several feet into the formation; generally considered a measurement of the undisturbed formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Deep Induction Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity, measured by an induction log, which represents a measurement made several feet into the formation; generally considered a measurement of the undisturbed formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Deep Lateral Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity measurement using a "lateral" electrode arrangement with a "deep" investigation radius (several feet into the formation).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Deep Laterolog Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity, measured by a laterolog (or guard log) resistivity device, which represents a measurement made several feet into the formation; generally considered a measurement of the undisturbed formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Dielectric Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity measurement which has been compensated for the dielectric constant of the formation..

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Propagation Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Formation resistivity as measured by the attenuation or phase shift of a high frequency electromagnetic wave; the frequency range for these measurements is higher than that of induction measurements, typically hundreds of KHz to several MHz, and over 1 GHz in the case of the Schlumberger EPT tool.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Phase Shift Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Formation resistivity as measured by the phase shift of a high frequency electromagnetic wave (hundreds of KHz to several MHz, 1.1 GHz in the case of Schlumberger's EPT tool); these measurements are typically sharp (good vertical resolution) and have good dynamic range, but their depth of investigation is less than that of measurements based on attenuation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Attenuation Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Formation resistivity as measured by the attenuation of a high frequency (hundreds of KHz to several MHz) electromagnetic wave; these measurements are typically deeper than measurements based on phase shift, but their vertical resolution is less sharp and they often cannot be used reliably in high-resistivity formations.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Flushed Zone Resistivity (Rxo)
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of the formation flushed zone (that portion of the formation in which the movable fluids are considered to have been completely replaced by mud filtrate during drilling).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Formation Resistivity (Rt)
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: True Formation Resistivity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Horizontal Resistivity (Rh)
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Formation resistivity measured parallel to layering. (for "Transverse-Isotropic (TI)" rock"

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Vertical Resistivity (Rv)
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Formation resistivity measured perpendicular to layering. (for "Transverse-Isotropic (TI)" rock

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Ro
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of formation, assuming 100% water-saturated.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Filter Cake Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of Mud Filter Cake

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of a fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Impedance Factor
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Impedance Factor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Annulus Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of the invasion annulus, a region of the formation lying between the flushed zone and the undisturbed formation, and filled with interstitial water displaced from the flushed zone.)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of Drilling Fluid, also known as mud.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottomhole Mud Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of the mud at Bottomhole Conditions

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Medium Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity which represents a measurement made approximately two to three feet into the formation; generally considered to measure the formation where it contain fluids which are a mixture of mud filtrate, connate water and possibly hydrocarbons.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Medium Induction Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity, made by an induction log, which represents a measurement made approximately two to three feet into the formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Medium Lateral Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity measurement using a "lateral" electrode arrangement with a "medium" investigation radius (~a foot or two into the formation).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Medium Laterolog Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity, measured by a laterolog (or guard log) resistivity device, which represents a measurement made approximately two to three feet into the formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Micro Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measurement of the resistivity of the formation within the first few inches of the borehole wall.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Micro Spherically Focused Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measurement of the resistivity of the formation, by a spherically focused tool, within the first few inches of the borehole wall.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Micro Cylindrically Focused Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measurement of the resistivity of the formation, by a cylindrically focused tool, within the first few inches of the borehole wall.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Micro Inverse Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Micro Resistivity measurement using an "inverse" lateral electrode arrangement; traditionally combined with Micro Normal Resistivity in a Microlog survey for identifying permeable beds.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Micro Lateral Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity measurement using a "lateral" electrode arrangement with a very shallow investigation radius (1-2 inches into the formation).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Micro Laterolog Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measurement of the resistivity of the formation, by a laterolog (or guard log) resistivity device, within the first few inches of the borehole wall.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Micro Normal Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Micro Resistivity measurement using a "normal" electrode arrangement; traditionally combined with Micro Inverse Resistivity in a Microlog survey for identifying permeable beds.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mineral Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Mineral Resistivity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Filtrate Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of mud filtrate

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Apparent Mud Filtrate Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Apparent resistivity of the mud filtrate, generally from log measurements of the "flushed zone".

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Resistivity Profile
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity profile measurement, used primarily for pattern recognition; may or may not be calibrated.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shallow Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity which represents a measurement made approximately one to two feet into the formation; generally considered to measure the formation where it contains fluids which are comprised primarily of mud filtrate.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Spherically Focused Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity, measured by a spherically focused log, which represents the resistivity approximately one to two feet into the formation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shallow Induction Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity, measured by an induction log, which represents a measurement made approximately one to two feet into the formation; generally considered to measure the formation where it contains fluids which are comprised primarily of mud filtrate.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shallow Lateral Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity measurement using a "lateral" electrode arrangement with a "shallow" investigation radius (several inches into the formation).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shallow Laterolog Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The resistivity, measured by a laterolog (or guard log) resistivity device, which represents a measurement made approximately one to two feet into the formation; generally considered to measure the formation where it contains fluids which are comprised primarily of mud filtrate.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Short Normal Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Shallow Resistivity measurement using a "normal" electrode arrangement.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Water Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Resistivity of connate (formation) water

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Apparent Water Resistivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Apparent resistivity of connate (formation) water, generally from logs; such estimates require correction before they can be used quantitatively.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Borehole Drift Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The change in the borehole drift per length, usually referring to the borehole measured depth.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Dog_Leg_Severity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Curvature of the borehole over a standard length

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: DogLegSeverity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Curvature of the borehole over a standard length

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Curvature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the degree to which a path is curved relative to the length of the path along the curve.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inclination Build Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of change in inclination expressed in degrees per unit of course length.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Azimuth Turn Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of change of the azimuth of the borehole, normally expressed in degrees per unit of course length

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Rotation Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the rotation of an object per unit length; e.g., flowmeter rotation per length of pipe, pipe rotation per unit length (for stuck pipe applications.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Small Rotation Per Length
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Angle of rotation per unit of length for small quantities

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Angular Acceleration
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of change of angular velocity per unit of time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Angular Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Rotation rate, usually measured in revolutions per unit time; e.g., spinner speed, motor speed, etc. The term Angular Frequency is also used, but generally refers to data scaled in radians per second.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Rotary Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Rotational speed of the Rotary Table.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bit Rotation Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Rotational speed of the Drill Bit

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Centrifuge Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The bowl speed of a centrifuge.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bowl Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The bowl speed of a centrifuge.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Differential Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The differential speed between the bowl and the conveyor of a centrifuge.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Motor Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rotational speed of a motor.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Spinner Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Rotational speed of the flowmeter spinner.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tool Rotation Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Rotational speed of the logging tool

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Conicity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The solid angle measuring the degree of resemblance of a solid to a cone especially in shape.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Activation Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature at which recording should begin

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Boiling Point Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature at which fractions of a liquid boil.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottomhole Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature at the bottom of a borehole occurring at the time of the activity being performed on the well.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: BHCT
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The bottom hole temperature reached when circulating. Due to the cooling effect of the drill fluid, BHCT is below the BHST.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottomhole Flowing Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature at the bottom of the well while flowing.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: BHST
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The bottom hole equilibrium temperature (when circulation is stopped)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bubble Point Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature at reservoir conditions at which gas in solution in crude oil comes out of solution as free gas.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Coolant Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of the cooling fluid

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Critical Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The highest temperature at which a fluid can exist as a liquid and above which its vapor cannot be liquefied regardless of the amount of pressure. Applies to pure components; for mixtures use Pseudocritical_Temperature.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Critical Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The highest temperature at which a gas can exist as a liquid and above which its vapor cannot be liquefied regardless of the amount of pressure (Dry gas = free gas without condensate)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pseudocritical Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The highest temperature at which a fluid can exist as a liquid and above which its vapor cannot be liquefied regardless of the amount of pressure. Used for mixtures, analogous to Critical_Temperature for pure components.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wet Gas Critical Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The highest temperature at which the gas can exist as a liquid and above which its vapor cannot be liquefied regardless of the amount of pressure (Wet gas - mixture of free gas plus condensate)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Differential Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The difference in temperature between two objects or materials.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Engine Oil Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Engine lubrication Oil Temperature

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fann Test Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature at which the Fann test was performed.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Formation Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of the (earth) formations.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Final Transfer Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Final temperature of shipping bottle

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature of a fluid (sample) under certain conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature of a mud or drilling fluid (sample) under certain conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Oil Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature of oil under certain conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Borehole Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of the material in the borehole.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Annulus Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of the fluid in the annulus. The annulus is the region outside the subject pipe, such as the region between drill pipe and the formation, or between casing and formation, or between tubing and casing.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gel Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of gelled fluid (fracturing gel, gelled acid ...)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Hydraulic Drive Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of the hydraulic fluid delivered to an Hydraulic motor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Initial Reservoir Pressure Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature taken when initial reservoir pressure recorded

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Operating Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum operating temperature for an equipment item.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Max Storage Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum Storage Temperature

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Max Surge Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum Temperature to which this Equipment can be exposed for a short time without permanent damage; the Equipment will again perform to specifications when the Temperature is reduced below the maximum working temperature.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum temperature

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Temperature Reached
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum temperature reached by the system, sensor or equipment

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Min Storage Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Minimum Storage Temperature

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Orifice Meter Gas Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of gas at orifice meter line when a sample is taken

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Separator Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of the separator when a sample is taken

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Surface Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature above ground. Temperature of the atmosphere.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Standard Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature considered to be "standard", for rates and volumes reported to be measured at Standard Conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Temperature In
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature of the input material.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Temperature Out
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature of the output material

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Temperature Sensor Resolution
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The minimum significant temperature change that can be detected above the noise. This is measured as the standard deviation of the differences between two successive measurements.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tool Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Internal temperature of the logging tool

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Vertical Lift Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Computed temperature at some depth in tubing

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wellhead Flowing Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature at the Wellhead with well flowing

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wellhead Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The temperature at the wellhead occurring at the time of the activity being performed on the well.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wind-chill
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the combined chilling effect of wind and low temperature on living things, also named chill factor, e.g., according to US weather service table, an air temperature of 30 degF with a 10 mi/h corresponds to a "wind-chill" of 22 degF.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Working Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature at which an equipment item normally operates

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Working Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Recommended maximum temperature at which equipment can be used

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Working Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Recommended minimum temperature at which equipment can be used

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sensor Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Temperature of a specific sensor.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Thermal Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of change of temperature with length.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Geothermal Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of change of temperature with depth in the Earth. It averages about 30 degC/km at shallow depths.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Well Thermal Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of change of temperature with measured depth in a well; equivalent to Geothermal_Gradient for a vertical well whose temperature has stabilized.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Geo_Thermal_Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of increase in temperature per unit depth in the Earth

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: GeoThermalGradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate of increase in temperature per unit depth in the Earth

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Temperature Per Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Added by Jerome Alperovitch (SRPC) 12-Jun-95

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Temperature Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the rate at which temperature varies per time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Rock Thermal Conductivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Rock thermal conductivity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Slew Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Highest rate of change in signal level which a device can produce; also the rate at which a device reacts to commands. In the latter case, the data are normally represented in units of time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Day
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Hardwires day (d) as unit.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Absolute Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A time value which is intended to fix an event in time, such as a geological time, a date, or the start time of a process.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Begin Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time at which a process began

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date, usually expressed in the format of the DBMS; e.g., Oracle date format is dd-mm-yy.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Core Sample Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date on which the core was recovered.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Date Created
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date of creation of a data item in the database.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Effective Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date on which a contract becomes effective or put in force.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: End Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date/time of the end of an activity.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Event Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date of an event.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Execution Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date that a contract is executed, usually the date of signing of the last signatory

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Expiration Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Expiration date of a legal document or an item.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Expiry Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date at which a contract terminates or is no longer in force. If the expiry date is amended, this is the amended date.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Original Expiry Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The original date that the contract was to terminate. If the contract is extended, this date does not change.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Date Placed in Service
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date on which an equipment item or product was placed in service.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Grading Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date on which the grading of equipment condition or state took place.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Date of Initial Reservoir Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date when initial reservoir pressure data were recorded

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Calibration Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date when a sensor was last calibrated

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Load Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date data was loaded

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Magnetic Declination Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Effective date and time at which the magnetic declination value has become valid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Model Year
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The year or full date of a model usually of an equipment item.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Date Modified
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date of modification of a data item in the database.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Publication Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date of publication of a document.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Report Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date (time) when report was completed or issued.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sale Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date of lease purchase

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Service Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date on which a service was performed.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Spud Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date a spud attempt was performed on a well

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Start Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date/time a particular activity started.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Start of Sampling
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Starting date/time of surface sampling

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Date Of Static Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date when Static Pressure data were recorded

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stop Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date a particular activity stopped.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Termination Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date on which a lease, an organization, or any legal or organizational entity was terminated.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Test Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date at which a particular test activity was conducted.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Total Depth Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The date/time at which the drilling reached total depth.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Abandonment Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time that a reservoir was or is anticipated to be abandoned.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Award Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date lease awarded

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Calibration Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date of calibration for the equipment; time may also be included.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Completion Date
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Date that the activities that created the wellbore were completed and the wellbore was available to produce gas or oil, or for other intended service (e.g. gas storage, geothermal, etc.). Common completion activities include running and cementing the "production string" of casing, perforating the casing and cement sheath, installing the production string (tubing, packers, etc.) and the wellhead, etc.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: End Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time at which a process ended

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: End of Sampling
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: End date/time of surface sampling

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sensor End Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: End time (tend) as observed by downhole or surface sensors, measured as elapsed time since the Time Reference.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time at End of Transient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: End time (tend) of the Transient

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Window End Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: End time of the processing window.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Geologic Age
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The geochronologic age of an item or event, such as an earth layer. This is usually the average age in millions of years (Ma).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Start Geologic Age
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The earliest (numerically largest) geologic or geochronologic age associated with an event or item, such as an earth layer, a fossil or pollen type.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: End Geologic Age
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The latest (numerically smallest) geologic or geochronologic age associated with an event or item, such as an earth layer, a fossil or pollen type.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Reference Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Reference Date and Time For Elapsed Time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Production History Reference Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Reference Date and Time for Production History

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Start Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time a certain activity or sub-activity started. Use Start_Age for geochronological time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time at Start of Transient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Start time (t0) of the Transient

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Window Start Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Start time of the processing window.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Power Supply Start Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Actual date and time at which the recorder was powered on.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Scheduled Start Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Scheduled start time for an activity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sensor Start Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Start time (t0) as observed by downhole or surface sensors, measured as elapsed time since the Time Reference.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stop Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time a certain activity or sub-activity stopped.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Stamp
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A time value which is associated with some event to fix its occurrence in time; often expressed as an elapsed time from recent reference time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Anelasticity Factor
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Factor used to compute loss of wave energy due to anelasticity (deviation from a linear proportionality between stress and strain). Loss is computed as exp(-pi * f * Anelasticity_Factor).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Energy Half Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time, within a specified interval, at which half the energy of the interval occurs

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Marsh Funnel Viscosity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time needed for a given quantity of fluid (generally a quart of mud) to flow into a specified size funnel (3/16 inch id tube of a 12 inch long funnel). Used for drilling fluids.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Station Residual Static
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Residual static information (time) for each station

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tau
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time for the neutron population to fall to 1/e (37%) of its original value. Commonly called Tau, it is inversely related to Neutron_Capture_Cross_Section

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Interval
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A time value which is intended to indicate the duration of a process or event.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Of First Data
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Listening time until first detection

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time System Offset Wrt Standard Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time zone correction (defined to fractions of an hour) to be added to vehicle system time to correct to standard time. (GMT, UTC,...)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tracking Operator Length
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Length (time or depth interval) of the crosscorrelation window to use while tracking

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tracking Window Bottom
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Interval below the picked Z to search for the Tracking Event and Snap_Type while tracking

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tracking Window Top
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Interval above the picked Z to search for the Tracking Event and Snap_Type while tracking

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transfer Duration
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Duration of sampling operation

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time required for a wave to travel from one point to another.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time Ampmod
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transit time estimated from processing

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time Initial
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Initial transit time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time NMO
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Normal moveout transit time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time Nominal
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Nominal transit time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time Qfactor
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transit time q-factor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time SRD
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transit time with respect to seismic reference datum

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time Sensor
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transit time taken from tool sensor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time Shear
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Shear wave transit time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transit Time Slope
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transit time slope

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acquisition Transit Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acquisition system transit time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Pick
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic transit time (normally a two-way time) from seismic reference datum to the well marker, as picked from a seismic section.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Trough Peak Delta Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time difference between trough and peak

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Trough Trough Delta Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time difference between two troughs

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Thickness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Vertical time difference between layers.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wave Period
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average elapsed time between the passing of two wave peaks.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Payout Period
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time in which all costs of leasing, exploring, drilling and operating have been recovered from production of a well or wells as defined by contractual agreement

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acoustic Travel Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The elapsed time required for an acoustic wave to travel from one point to another.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Integrated Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Total acoustic travel time over a wellbore interval as computed by integrating acoustic slowness from a sonic log (Compressional_Slowness) over the interval.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: One Way Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time required for an acoustic wave to travel directly from one point to another; used to distinguish from Two_Way_Time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Two Way Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time required for an acoustic wave to travel from its source to a reflector and return to a receiver.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Interpretation
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Generic interpretation on seismic traveltime sections

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Migrated Time Interpretation
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Seismic travel time interpretation based on migrated sections; typically represented as a grid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stacked Time Interpretation
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Seismic traveltime interpretation based on stacked seismic sections

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Top Two Way Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Depth of Top of Interval in Two Way Time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bottom Two Way Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Depth of Bottom of Interval in Two Way Time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Map Modeled Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Two-way time obtained through map modeling of depth surface data

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acquisition Break Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acquisition system break time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acquisition Shot Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acquisition system shot time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Aperture Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time interval which contains the data used in a calculation, usually specified as the start and end times for the aperture.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Battery Life
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Battery Life

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Current Equivalent Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Computed equivalent operating time based on the time spent at a given temperature and the maximum working temperature. If all the time is spent at maximum working temperature, then the equivalent time is equal to the operating time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Equivalent Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cumulative Equivalent Operating Time, called Cumulative Time Usage or CTU.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Delay Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time difference by which one event lags another. In refraction seismic work, the additional time required to traverse a raypath over the time which would be required to traverse the horizontal component at the highest velocity encountered on the raypath.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Max Delay Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum Delay Time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Min Delay Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Minimum Delay Time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time After Bit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Toolface Time After Bit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and the point at which the toolface measurement is taken reaching a given point in the wellbore.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Density Time After Bit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a density sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gamma Ray Time After Bit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a gamma ray sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Neutron Time After Bit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a neutron sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Resistivity Time After Bit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a resistivity sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sonic Time After Bit
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a sonic sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Downtime
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time during which equipment is not operational condition or is otherwise unavailable.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Drift Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The difference between actual acoustic travel time to a subsurface point (as measured in a check shot survey) and the integrated acoustic slowness from sonic logging data.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Duration
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Elapsed time from the start to the finish of a process or activity.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Session Duration
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Elapsed time from the start to the finish of a recording or processing session.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Term
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Term of an agreement. Usually in years

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Warmup Duration
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Duration between power-on time and acquisition start time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Event Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time of an event, such as a pick time from a waveform, expressed as the elapsed time from a chosen "zero" time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Event Time 0
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Event Time 0

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Event Time 1
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Event Time 1

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Event Time 2
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Event Time 2

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Event Time 3
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Event Time 3

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Event Time 4
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Event Time 4

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Ideal Sample Shift 0
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Fractional sample shift associated with ideal position 0

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Ideal Sample Shift 1
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Fractional sample shift associated with ideal position 1

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Ideal Sample Shift 2
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Fractional sample shift associated with ideal position 2

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Idle Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Period of time during which equipment is idle. Complement of Operating_Time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Closure Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time required by a hydraulic fracture to close. Can be derived from a Nolte plot (pressure vs. time). The more fluid that fluid leaks off into the formation, the faster the fracture closes.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Intermediate Time Level
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Seismic line dependent adjustment to achieve a continuous, line independent reference surface

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time difference between two reflection events. It may vary due to velocity changes in different media, or changes in thickness of strata, or changes following erosion or structural deformation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Extreme Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum time at extreme conditions

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Min Scan Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Scan Time corresponding to the fastest scanning rate supported by the Equipment

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mis-tie Phase Time Equivalent
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Equivalent time correction corresponding to the phase corrections. Assumes a specified dominant frequency.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mis-tie Static Correction Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Constant time correction to apply to a seismic line to compensate for time differences.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mis-tie Variable Correction Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time correction applicable to each trace on a seismic line.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Normal Moveout
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The additional time required for energy to travel from a source to a flat reflecting bed and back to a geophone at some distance from the source point compared to the time to return to a geophone at the source point.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Operating Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Period of time which is spent operating, either for a single operation or for a series of operations. Complement of Idle_Time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pumping Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Elapsed time during which pumping has taken place.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Relative Pumping Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time it takes to pump fluid into the fracture

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bit Operating Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Operating time of the bit over the reporting period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Drilling Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Elapsed time during which drilling has taken place.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Engine Total Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time spent by an engine in operating condition since the last overhaul.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Expected Life
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Expected operating time of the equipment, generally defined as operating time of the first failure for 95% of the equipment

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Jar Operating Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Operating time of the jar over the reporting period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: LWD Operating Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Operating time of the logging-while-drilling (LWD) equipment over the reporting period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: MWD Operating Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Operating time of the MWD equipment over the reporting period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Motor Operating Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Operating time of the motor over the reporting period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Peak Peak Delta Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time difference between two peaks.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Peak Trough Delta Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time difference between peak and trough.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Period
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time T for one cycle of a periodic function. The time for a wave crest to traverse a distance equal to one wavelength. The reciprocal of Frequency.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Relaxation Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In nuclear magnetic resonance measurements, the time constant related to the rate at which nuclei realign to the static magnetic field after disturbance by a radio frequency pulse.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Relaxation Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transverse, or spin-spin, relaxation time constant for transverse magnetization decay rate of nuclei; normally abbreviated by symbol T2.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Relaxation Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Longitudinal, or spin-lattice, relaxation time constant for alignment rate of nuclei to static magnetic field; normally abbreviated by symbol T1.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Window Length (Time)
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Length of window in time domain

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Ramping Duration
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time duration of the ramp tapering the time window

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Receiver Event First Arrival
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time of arrival of first break for each receiver event

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Receiver Station Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time of first measurement for each station since the Origin_Time stored in Seis_Survey_Area

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Recorder Delay Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Delay time between instrument power-on time and when recording begins

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Reduced Traveltime
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Difference between observed refraction traveltime and the traveltime which would have been observed if only one head-wave velocity had been involved.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sampling Period
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Duration of data sampling or recording.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sampling Period
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time interval between the recording of two sequential data samples.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sliding Window Duration
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Duration (length) in time of the sliding window used for processing.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Snap Window Bottom
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Interval below the picked Z to search for the Tracking Event and Snap_Type when snapping

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Snap Window Top
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Interval above the picked Z to search for the Tracking Event and Snap_Type when snapping

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Elapsed Time at Stable Conditions
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time elapsed since production conditions were stable

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Total Mis-tie Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Total amount of mis-tie correction to apply. Evaluated at line ties.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Increment
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time increment between samples indexed by time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Uncertainty
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Uncertainty of a time measurement.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Constant
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Exponential decay time constant, also known as mean lifetime, tau and inverse of decay constant (lambda)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Simulation Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Simulation time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inverse Penetration Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Inverse of drilling penetration rate.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: InversePenetrationRate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Use for Inverse ROP measurements

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acoustic Slowness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The transit time interval per unit length of an acoustic wave; inverse of wave velocity. Applies to all types of Delta-T: Compressional, Shear and Stoneley.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Compressional Slowness
