ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time it takes for a compressional wave to traverse a fixed distance; reciprocal of Compressional_Velocity.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic slowness of a fluid; the slowness of the compressional wave.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mud Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic compressional slowness (Delta-T) of the drilling fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Matrix Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic slowness of a compressional wave in a given material or matrix.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Rayleigh Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The acoustic slowness of a Rayleigh wave (type of seismic wave propagated along the free surface of a semi-infinite medium).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shear Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic slowness of a shear wave (Vs); reciprocal of Shear_Velocity; a shear wave is a type of seismic wave in which the particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of propagation; also called S-wave or secondary wave.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Matrix Shear Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic slowness of a shear wave in a given material or matrix.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stoneley Delta-T
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The acoustic slowness of a Stoneley wave; a Stoneley wave is a type of seismic wave which is propagated along an interface, such as a tube wave in a borehole.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Low Acoustic Slowness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic slowness for small quantities

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Electromagnetic Propagation Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Time per unit length required for an electromagnetic wave to propagate over some interval in some medium like air, water, drilling fluid, etc..

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Matrix Electromagnetic Propagation Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The time it takes for an electromagnetic wave to traverse a fixed distance of a given material or matrix. In this case the material or matrix is a specific, zero porosity rock, e.g. sandstone, limestone or dolomite.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Transit Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The travel time of a wave over a unit distance, hence the reciprocal of wave velocity.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Time Dip
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Dip computed on a time surface by measuring the difference in seismic times between two points compared to the horizontal distance between the points.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Correlation Time Dip
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Dip of seismic data, similar to Time_Dip but gradient derived from the seismic data in time)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Litho Penetration Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate at which a drill bit penetrates a particular lithostratigraphic layer; measured in units of time per mass.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gas D Factor
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Gas D factor

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Weather_Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Use for wind and current speeds

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: WeatherSpeed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Use for wind and current speeds

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: NMR_Surface_Relaxivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: NMR surface relaxivity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acoustic Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity of an acoustic wave; the rate at which the wave travels from one point to another. Used generally for all elastic and seismic waves.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acoustic Dispersion
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Variation of acoustic velocity with frequency. Dispersion may be normal (velocity decreases with frequency) or inverse (velocity increases with frequency).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Angular Dispersion
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Variation of acoustic velocity with direction, distorting the shape of a wavetrain.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Apparent Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In seismics, the phase velocity which a wavefront appears to have along a line of geophones. Otherwise, the inverse of the slope of a refraction time-distance curve.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Average Acoustic Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average velocity of an acoustic wave: the distance between two points divided by the travel time of the compressional wave between those points.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Average Seismic Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Special usage of Avg_Acoustic_Velocity which deals specifically with the velocity between a reference datum near the surface and some subsurface point; often a vertical path is implied and the velocity is computed as depth divided by seismic travel time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average velocity in a layer or between two subsurface points; generally applied to a rock layer whose velocity can be considered homogeneous. May be derived from stacking velocity using the Dix equation (or a more refined variant).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Compressional Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Velocity of a compressional acoustic wave (Vp).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Compressional Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic velocity of an acoustic (compressional) wave in fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Matrix Compressional Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic velocity of a compressional wave in a given material or matrix.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gas Acoustic Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Sound velocity of gas at reservoir pressure and temperature. Typical value is 200 m/s.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Group Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity with which the energy in a wavetrain travels. In dispersive media, it is the velocity of the envelope of the wavetrain.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Ray Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity in the direction of energy transport; in anisotropic media it is different from the direction in which the phase velocity is measured. Also called group velocity.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Migration Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Velocity applied in seismic migration.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mode Converted Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Converted-wave velocity corresponding to a Compressional wave traveling in one direction and a Shear wave traveling the opposite direction, with conversion at the reflector.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stack Mode Converted Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Stacking converted-wave velocity, for a wave traveling through layers as a Compressional wave in one direction and a Shear wave in the other. This can be computed from a combined RMS average of the Compressional and Shear interval velocities. In practice it is usually determined directly from velocity analysis on short offset converted wave data.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Average Mode Converted Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average converted-wave velocity from the surface to the reflector. The converted wave velocity is determined from the time taken for the energy to travel in one direction as compressional wave and in the other as shear.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Mode Converted Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Converted-wave velocity measured over a finite interval, with the interval usually determined by geologic layering. The converted wave velocity is determined from the time taken for the energy to travel in one direction as Compressional wave and in the other as Shear.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Phase Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity of any given phase (such as a trough) or a wave of single frequency; may differ from Group Velocity due to dispersion in the medium.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Oil Acoustic Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Sound velocity of live oil at reservoir pressure and temperature. Typical value is 1000 m/s.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: RMS Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transit-time weighted root mean square of the interval velocities over a series if intervals.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Rayleigh Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity of a Rayleigh wave (type of seismic wave propagated along the free surface of a semi-infinite medium.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Shear Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity of a shear wave (Vs); a shear wave is a type of seismic wave in which the particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of propagation; also called S-wave or secondary wave.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stack Shear Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Stacking shear wave velocity computed from an RMS average of the Shear interval velocities. In practice it is often determined from velocity analysis on Shear wave data, or indirectly from the stacking velocities for Compressional and Converted wave data.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Average Shear Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average shear wave velocity, from the surface to the reflector. The shear wave velocity is determined from the two-way vertical time taken for the energy to travel to the reflector and back as a Shear wave.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Interval Shear Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Interval shear wave velocity, measured over a finite interval, with the interval usually determined by geologic layering.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Matrix Shear Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Acoustic velocity of a shear wave in a given material or matrix.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stacking Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity determined from velocity analysis based upon normal-moveout measurements.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stoneley Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity of a Stoneley wave; a Stoneley wave is a type of seismic wave which is propagated along an interface, such as a tube wave in a borehole.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Velocity at Z0
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: (Instantaneous) Velocity at surface reference z=0 (z is time or depth).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Velocity To SRD
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Velocity of the medium between the zero-time reference of a particular survey to the Seismic Reference Datum.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Velocity Uncertainty
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Uncertainty of a velocity measurement.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Acoustic Velocity of Water
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Sound velocity in water. Typical value under reservoir conditions is 1550 m/s.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Weathering Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average acoustic velocity of the weathered layer, the near-surface low velocity layer consisting of unconsolidated material and rock in which air rather than water fills the pore space.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Weathering Velocity at CDP
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Weathering velocity at a CDP.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cable Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cable speed, generally measured at the surface as an approximation of tool speed.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Corrosion Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate at which corrosion, a complex chemical or electrochemical process by which metal is destroyed, occurs. For example the rate at which a casing pipe rusts (corrodes).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Flow Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow velocity of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Apparent Fluid Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Apparent velocity of the fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Bubble Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate at which a fluid bubble, gas or liquid, flows through another fluid, gas or liquid. The Velocity depends on the densities and viscosities of the fluids.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gas Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow velocity of gas component of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Heavy Phase Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow velocity of heavy phase component of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Light Phase Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow velocity of light phase component of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Liquid Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow velocity of liquid component of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Oil Bubble Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Oil Bubble Velocity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Oil Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow velocity of oil component of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Slippage Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: In two-phase flow, the difference between the velocities of the two phases.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Water Bubble Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Water Bubble Velocity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Water Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow velocity of water component of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Erosional Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity of a flow below which erosional damage to devices such as completion equipment is minimized.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Displacement Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The velocity of the shock or displacement front.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Penetration Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Usually used to describe the rate at which a formation is penetrated during drilling operation. In general, the rate at which an equipment penetrates a surface or subsurface volume.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Average Penetration Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average drilling penetration rate (ROP)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Running Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Speed of an equipment running into (counted positive) or out of the hole (counted negative).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Average Running Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Average Speed of equipment running into (counted positive) or out of the hole (counted negative).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tool Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Speed of the tool; logging speed.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Tool Speed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Maximum service speed allowed for, or attained by, a logging tool.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wind Velocity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Velocity of the wind

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Liquid Flux per Area
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Liquid flux per area

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Erosion Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The rate at which erosion occurs.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Sedimentation Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The deposited thickness of sediments under the influence of gravity in a defined timeframe

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Volume Per Area Per Geologic Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Describes the volume per area per million years. E.g. the quantity of hydrocarbons generated in a particular area in a certain timeframe

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gas Production Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: This is a copy of the unit quantity GasProductionVolume, which acts as the parent for other SDM_Property instances

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Gas Production Volume Per Number Of Fractures
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Normalized gas cumulative per number of fractures

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Liquid Production Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: This is a copy of the unit quantity LiquidProductionVolume, which acts as the parent for other SDM_Property instances

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Water Production Volume Per Number Of Fractures
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Normalized water  cumulative per number of fractures

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Liquid Production Volume Per Number Of Fractures
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Normalized liquid cumulative per number of fractures

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Oil Production Volume Per Number Of Fractures
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Normalized oil cumulative per number of fractures

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Annulus Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The volume of the portion of the borehole which lies between the borehole wall and the casing.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Borehole Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The volume of the borehole.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Borehole Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cumulative volume of the borehole (integrated over length of borehole).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Borehole Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The estimated volume of the Open Hole used in fluid volume/placement computations

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cement Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of cement.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Cement Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cumulative volume of cement (may be integrated over length of borehole or over time of cementing operation).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Production Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of fluids produced by a zone or interval since the beginning of the production

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Water Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cumulative water production at standard conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Condensate Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cumulative condensate production.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Gas Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cumulative gas production at standard conditions. At constant BHP or WHP, cumulative volume is not the straightforward sum of volume by RHU but determined by Inverse Laplace transformation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Oil Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Cumulative oil production at standard conditions. At constant BHP or WHP, cumulative volume is not the straightforward sum of volume by RHU but determined by Inverse Laplace transformation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The cumulative volume, typically of a fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Cumulative Water Influx
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The cumulative volume of water that encroaches into a reservoir.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Dead Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of material remaining in a container after normal emptying procedure, and thus not available for use.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Displacing Fluid Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of fluid used to displace another fluid. In special core analysis, may be expressed as unitless multiple of pore volume.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Drilling Fluid Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of drilling fluid

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Loss
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of filtrate, such as recovered from an API Fluid Loss test. API RP13 Section 3

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: HTHP Fluid Loss
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of filtrate produced under high temperature, high pressure (HTHP) conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: LTLP Fluid Loss
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of filtrate produced under low temperature, low pressure (LTLP) conditions.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Loss
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The volume of drilling fluid filtrate which is obtained in a filtration test under specific test conditions; used as an indication of the expected rate of filtrate invasion into the formation during drilling.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fluid Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of fluid.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Fracture Conductivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Fracture permeability - width product of a finite conductivity vertical or horizontal fracture.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Initial Gas Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of gas accumulated prior to the beginning of the measurement period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Initial Gas In Place
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Total volume of in situ gas in the reservoir.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Initial Oil In Place
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Total volume of in situ oil in the reservoir.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Initial Oil Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of oil accumulated prior to the beginning of the measurement period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Initial Water Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of water accumulated prior to the beginning of the measurement period.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Kick Tolerance Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Estimate of the volume of a kick (influx of fluid into the wellbore) at bottom hole conditions which can be shut in and circulated out without breaking the formation

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Matrix Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The volume of material in a porous system that does not include the volume of the pores.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Maximum Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The maximum volume not to be exceeded for a container (Tank, Mud Pit)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mf Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Amount of 0.02 normal (N/50) standard sulfuric acid required in order to turn the color of methyl orange indicator solution from yellow to pink when determining methyl orange alkalinity of the mud filtrate, Mf, API RP13 Section 8, Chemical Analysis.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Nominal Liquid Capacity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of fluid which can be contained in the vessel

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Permeability Thickness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The product of permeability and thickness of the body acting as a conduit.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Total Permeability Thickness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Total permeability-thickness [= kh(1) + kh(2)] for a vertical interference test

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Net Pay Permeability Thickness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Thickness of the permeable net pay portion of the zone i.e., the product of the Net Pay Thickness and Net Pay Average Permeability

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Net Reservoir Permeability Thickness
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The product of the Net Reservoir Thickness and Net Reservoir Average Permeability.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pf Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Amount of 0.02 normal (N/50) standard sulfuric acid required in order to turn the color of phenolphthalein indicator solution from pink to colorless when determining phenolphthalein alkalinity of the mud filtrate, Pf, API RP13 Section 8, Chemical Analysis.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pm Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Amount of 0.02 normal (N/50) standard sulfuric acid required in order to turn the color of phenolphthalein indicator solution from pink to colorless when determining phenolphthalein alkalinity of the mud, Pm, API RP13 Section 8, Chemical Analysis.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pore Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The volume within a geologic volume that describes the connected void space within the matrix of rock.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Hydrocarbon Pore Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The pore volume of a reservoir occupied by hydrocarbons in either the vapor or liquid phase.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Remaining Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of material which remains (e.g. remaining volume to be pumped)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Rat Hole Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Available volume of fluids below testing valve. The rat hole is the section of the borehole running from the tester valve to the effective bottom of the well. The calculation of this volume is not straight-forward as the rat hole is not generally empty.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stroke Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of a pump stroke

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Surface Lines Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Total volume of the surface lines equipment

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Stage Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of material pumped during a stage of an activity.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Displacement Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Dead volume including the surface treating lines to be pumped to move the treating fluid down to formation. In cementing it is the volume (through casing/tubing/ drillpipe) up to the landing collar; in acidizing it is the tubing volume to perforations

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Volumetric Coefficient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Multiplicative factor (Volume per pulse), sometimes called K Factor.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Reservoir Production Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Reservoir production volume

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Transmissibility
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Transmissibility

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Critical Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The inverse of density at the critical point of a fluid, describing the volume occupied by a fluid of unit mass.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Specific Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the volume distribution of a gas or liquid per unit mass.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: gas volume per mass
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of gas production per mass

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Coal gas volume per mass
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume of gas production per mass in coal, for example the Langmuir volume constant.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Adsorption Volume Per Mass
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Adsorbed volume of hydrocarbon components per rock mass

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: System Compliance
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The internal volume change of a fluidic system per pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Wellbore Storage
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Measure of the ability of the wellbore to store fluid ("afterflow" when a well is shut in) or unload fluid (when a well is opened to flow).

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Generation Rate Per Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Describes the generation of hydrocarbons from kerogen in dependency to temperature

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Magnetic Flux Density Gradient
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: A measure of the change in magnetic flux density per unit length.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Counterion Conductivity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Added to support unit "(S/m)/(meq/cm3)"

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Energy Per Mass
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Energy absorbed, contained or produced per unit of mass

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Absorbed Dose
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Absorbed dose is a measure of the energy deposited in a medium by ionizing radiation.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Specific Energy
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Energy per unit mass, an intensive property in contrast to Energy as the extensive property

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Vaporization Heat
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The energy required to transform a given mass of a substance into a gas.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Energy Per Mass Per Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Energy absorbed, contained or produced per unit of mass per unit of time. Generalization of EquivalentDoseRate

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Equivalent Dose Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The amount of radioactivity in a substance of interest over time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Extensive Heat Capacity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Typically called HeatCapacity, but that name was taken and used as specific heat capacity; to distinguish from SpecificHeatCapacity the term Extensive has been added (See Wikipedia/Google)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Body Heat Capacity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a given body by one degree.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Extensive Heat Capacity Per Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Gradient of heat capacity per change in temperature. Note that this is not Heat Capacity per unit of mass (See definition of ExtensiveHeatCapacity)

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Flowrate Per Pressure Per Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Flow rate per pressure squared

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Compressible Fluid Productivity Index
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Productivity index for a compressible fluid, as a flow rate per pressure squared

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inverse Area
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Inverse of Area

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inverse Energy
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Inverse of Energy

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Molar Energy
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Energy absorbed, contained or produced per mole of a substance

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Molar Enthalpy
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Enthalpy per amount of substance

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Molar Heat Capacity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Heat capacity per mole of a substance

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Molar Mass
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The mass of one mole of a substance. Molar masses of specific isotopes and those based on average natural molecular weight are both in this unit dimension

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Molar Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The volume occupied by one mole of a substance at actual pressure and temperature.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mole Per Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Also called MolarRate

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Molar Rate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The amount of substance per unit of time.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Specific Heat Capacity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Supersedes previous HeatCapacity. This is the heat capacity per unit mass of a substance.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Heat Capacity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a unit volume of a given material by one degree.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Specific Heat Capacity Per Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Gradient of specific heat capacity per change in temperature. The temperature is a temperature difference, not an absolute temperature.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Heat Capacity per Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Heat capacity per unit temperature, see Heat_Capacity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Thermal Conduction Transmissibility
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Thermal conduction transmissibility

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Volumetric Heat Capacity
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Extensive heat capacity per volume

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Volumetric Heat Capacity Per Temperature
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Change in Volumetric Heat Capacity per change in temperature. The temperature is understood as temperature difference, not an absolute temperature.

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Per Flowrate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure per flow rate, inverse of FlowratePerPressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Per Liquid Flowrate
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure per flowrate for liquids

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Pressure Per Flowrate Squared
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Pressure per flowrate squared

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Inverse Temperature Squared
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Inverse of temperature squared

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Specific Heat Capacity Per Temperature Cubed
Heat capacity per unit temperature cubed
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Heat capacity per unit temperature cubed, see Heat_Capacity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Specific Heat Capacity Per Temperature Squared
Heat capacity per unit temperature squared
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Heat capacity per unit temperature squared, see Heat_Capacity

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mass Per Volume Per Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Mass per volume per time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Mass Rate Per Geologic Time
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Mass per volume per geologic time. E.g. the generated hydrocarbon mass per volume of rock per geologic time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Power Per Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Power per volume

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Heat Source
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Describes the heat generation related to radiogenic decay in a rock

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Square Root Pressure
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Square root pressure

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Square Root Energy Per Volume
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The Hildebrand solubility parameter is the square root of the cohesive energy density and used in petroleum systems to describe the solubility of hydrocarbon components in water

ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: Volume per mass per time

ListOfChildMeasurements.Name: Volume Rate Per Mass
ListOfChildMeasurements.Description: The volume per mass in geologic time. E.g. The volume of hydrocarbons generated by a mass of source rock in a geologic timeframe

WellknownMapStates.Description: Indicates that the mapsTo conversion factor is identical to the mapsFrom conversion factor. A copy of the value should be assigned the unit mapsTo. For deprecation state this indicates that the superseded item is identical.

Indicates that the mapsTo conversion factor has greater precision (i.e., changes in least significant digits). If there is knowledge that the value was converted from a different unit in the source dictionary, then consider using that conversion factor to reproduce the original value before converting to the target unit using a more precise target conversion factor. Otherwise, a copy of the value should be assigned the unit mapsTo. For deprecation state this indicates that the superseded item has higher precision.

Indicates that the mapsTo conversion factor represents a correction to the mapsFrom conversion factor. That is, the mapsFrom conversion factor has a problem. The value should be treated the same as for a state of precision. For deprecation state this indicates that the superseded item has corrected behavior.

A direct mapping is not specified, but the value can be converted to a supported item if the mapsFrom definition is presumed to be valid. For deprecation state this indicates that the current item can be converted to the superseded item if the current item is presumed to be valid.
Indicates a mapping to a similar alternative with a different underlying conversion factor in the less significant digits. Other mapping alternatives may be available.

A mapping is not specified because the underlying concept is not supported. For information on how to add a new concept to a dictionary, see http://w3.energistics.org/uom/Energistics_Unit_of_Measure_Usage_Guide_V1.pdf Section 5.1, page 17.

Similar to ‘corrected’ only that it isn’t as obvious who is wrong. This state is added by OSDD. Typical cases we cannot agree on are the year and the base unit for attenuation. Those are marked as different.
The exact definition is not found in the catalog. A temporary object (a unit or measurement) has been created as a substitute.
